thread:
alex_sales: Finwise POC seeing intermittent 502/503 and occasional TCP RSTs when traffic goes through their firewall + our PrivateLink interface after load spikes. Direct intra-AZ calls OK.

jamie_se: Are the errors 502 from our runtime or 503/timeouts? Any logs?

alex_sales: Mostly 502/503 at the app gateway, some RSTs seen.

katie_netops: Do they have a single interface endpoint in one AZ and route other AZs through it?

alex_sales: Yes, interface endpoint in us-west-2a; other AZs hitting it.

sam_eng_infra: Common problem: central SNAT + small ephemeral port range -> firewall session exhaustion. Also endpoints often return AZ-local IPs; cross-AZ hits can trigger ACLs.

jamie_se: We preserve source IPs on connector flows, right?

sam_eng_infra: Yes. But if they SNAT many clients to one IP before the firewall, it looks like tens of thousands of flows from one IP and the firewall can drop them.

katie_netops: Quick asks for Finwise: 1) confirm whether they're SNATing to a single egress IP, 2) verify ephemeral port range (recommend 1024-65535), 3) allow ephemeral ports from our endpoint IPs during POC. Recommend one NAT per AZ to spread source IPs.

alex_sales: I'll send that. Also they asked if VPC peering would help.

jamie_se: Peering can simplify routing but won't fix SNAT if they still use a central proxy/NAT. PrivateLink has endpoint-hour + per-GB costs; peering avoids endpoint charges but may incur cross-AZ transfer fees. Dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale.

katie_netops: Share this firewall example for POC:

```
ALLOW TCP 443 from <our-endpoint-ips> -> app-subnet
ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 from <our-endpoint-ips> -> app-subnet
ALLOW TCP 8050,9000 from <our-endpoint-ips> -> health-subnet
```

alex_sales: Action items I'll send: confirm NAT & ephemeral ports, open firewall to 1024-65535 for our endpoint IPs for testing, consider per-AZ NAT or peering if they want to avoid endpoint quirks, and provide tcpdump if issue continues.
